==Overview== {{Infobox religious building | name = Tamura Shrine (田村神社) | image = File:Tamura jinja Honden.jpg | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] [[:en:Kōka, Shiga|Kōka City]] [[:en:Tsuchiyama, Shiga|Tsuchiyama Town]] {{ill|Kitatsuchiyama|de|Kitatsuchiyama|ja|土山町北土山|zh|土山町北土山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitatsuchiyama|qq=|1=Kitatsuchiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86737193}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.93056|N|136.29833|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|WD=Q941979}} | shrine_ranking = Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|de|Präfektur‑Schrein|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|县社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/prefectural shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | established = Legendary: 3rd year of Kōnin (812) | main_shrine = Three‑bay [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|nagare‑zukuri]] | pilgrimage_site = {{ill|Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|de|Pilgerweg 134|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道 第134番|zh|神仏灵场巡拜之道 第134番|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2nd in Shiga) | annual_festival = [[:en:April 8|April 8]] | prefecture= {{ill|Koka|WD=Q847584}} }}
<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|qq=|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|qq=|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|qq=|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|qq=|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|qq=|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Festivals == * Monthly ** Monthly festival (18th of each month) * January ** New Year service (January 1) ** New Year grand prayer (January 1–7) * February ** National Foundation Day service (February 11) ** Great Exorcism Festival (February 17–19) * April ** Annual festival (April 8) * June ** Great Purification (June 30) * July ** Lantern festival (July 25–27) ** Children’s lantern float offering (July 25) ** Great festival of purification (July 26) ** Great festival of the people’s association (July 26) ** Lantern dedication safety prayer (July 27) * October–November ** Shichi‑Go‑San prayers (October, November) * November ** Harvest festival (November 23) * December ** Emperor’s birthday festival (December 23) ** Year-end purification and New Year’s Eve festival (December 31)
== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.

==Overview== {{Infobox religious building | name = Tamura Shrine (田村神社) | image = File:Tamura jinja Honden.jpg | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] [[:en:Kōka, Shiga|Kōka City]] [[:en:Tsuchiyama, Shiga|Tsuchiyama Town]] {{ill|Kitatsuchiyama|de|Kitatsuchiyama|ja|土山町北土山|zh|土山町北土山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitatsuchiyama|1=Kitatsuchiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86737193}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.93056|N|136.29833|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|WD=Q941979}} | shrine_ranking = Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|de|Präfektur‑Schrein|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|县社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | established = Legendary: 3rd year of Kōnin (812) | main_shrine = Three‑bay [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|nagare‑zukuri]] | pilgrimage_site = {{ill|Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|de|Pilgerweg 134|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道 第134番|zh|神仏灵场巡拜之道 第134番|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2nd in Shiga) | annual_festival = [[:en:April 8|April 8]] | prefecture= {{ill|Koka|WD=Q847584}} }}
<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Festivals == * Monthly ** Monthly festival (18th of each month) * January ** New Year service (January 1) ** New Year grand prayer (January 1–7) * February ** National Foundation Day service (February 11) ** Great Exorcism Festival (February 17–19) * April ** Annual festival (April 8) * June ** Great Purification (June 30) * July ** Lantern festival (July 25–27) ** Children’s lantern float offering (July 25) ** Great festival of purification (July 26) ** Great festival of the people’s association (July 26) ** Lantern dedication safety prayer (July 27) * October–November ** Shichi‑Go‑San prayers (October, November) * November ** Harvest festival (November 23) * December ** Emperor’s birthday festival (December 23) ** Year-end purification and New Year’s Eve festival (December 31)
== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.

==Overview== {{Infobox religious building | name = Tamura Shrine (田村神社) | image = File:Tamura jinja Honden.jpg | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] [[:en:Kōka, Shiga|Kōka City]] [[:en:Tsuchiyama, Shiga|Tsuchiyama Town]] {{ill|Kitatsuchiyama|de|Kitatsuchiyama|ja|土山町北土山|zh|土山町北土山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitatsuchiyama|1=Kitatsuchiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86737193}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.93056|N|136.29833|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|WD=Q941979}} | shrine_ranking = Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|de|Präfektur‑Schrein|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|县社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | established = Legendary: 3rd year of Kōnin (812) | main_shrine = Three‑bay [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|nagare‑zukuri]] | pilgrimage_site = {{ill|Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|de|Pilgerweg 134|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道 第134番|zh|神仏灵场巡拜之道 第134番|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2nd in Shiga) | annual_festival = [[:en:April 8|April 8]] | prefecture= {{ill|Koka|WD=Q847584}} }}
<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Festivals == * Monthly ** Monthly festival (18th of each month) * January ** New Year service (January 1) ** New Year grand prayer (January 1–7) * February ** National Foundation Day service (February 11) ** Great Exorcism Festival (February 17–19) * April ** Annual festival (April 8) * June ** Great Purification (June 30) * July ** Lantern festival (July 25–27) ** Children’s lantern float offering (July 25) ** Great festival of purification (July 26) ** Great festival of the people’s association (July 26) ** Lantern dedication safety prayer (July 27) * October–November ** Shichi‑Go‑San prayers (October, November) * November ** Harvest festival (November 23) * December ** Emperor’s birthday festival (December 23) ** Year-end purification and New Year’s Eve festival (December 31)
== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.

<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Festivals == * Monthly ** Monthly festival (18th of each month) * January ** New Year service (January 1) ** New Year grand prayer (January 1–7) * February ** National Foundation Day service (February 11) ** Great Exorcism Festival (February 17–19) * April ** Annual festival (April 8) * June ** Great Purification (June 30) * July ** Lantern festival (July 25–27) ** Children’s lantern float offering (July 25) ** Great festival of purification (July 26) ** Great festival of the people’s association (July 26) ** Lantern dedication safety prayer (July 27) * October–November ** Shichi‑Go‑San prayers (October, November) * November ** Harvest festival (November 23) * December ** Emperor’s birthday festival (December 23) ** Year-end purification and New Year’s Eve festival (December 31)
== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.

==Overview== {{Infobox religious building | name = Tamura Shrine (田村神社) | image = File:Tamura jinja Honden.jpg | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] [[:en:Kōka, Shiga|Kōka City]] [[:en:Tsuchiyama, Shiga|Tsuchiyama Town]] {{ill|Kitatsuchiyama|de|Kitatsuchiyama|ja|土山町北土山|zh|土山町北土山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitatsuchiyama|1=Kitatsuchiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86737193}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.93056|N|136.29833|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|WD=Q941979}} | shrine_ranking = Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|de|Präfektur‑Schrein|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|县社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | established = Legendary: 3rd year of Kōnin (812) | main_shrine = Three‑bay [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|nagare‑zukuri]] | pilgrimage_site = {{ill|Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|de|Pilgerweg 134|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道 第134番|zh|神仏灵场巡拜之道 第134番|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2nd in Shiga) | annual_festival = [[:en:April 8|April 8]] | prefecture= {{ill|Koka|WD=Q847584}} }}
<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Festivals == * Monthly ** Monthly festival (18th of each month) * January ** New Year service (January 1) ** New Year grand prayer (January 1–7) * February ** National Foundation Day service (February 11) ** Great Exorcism Festival (February 17–19) * April ** Annual festival (April 8) * June ** Great Purification (June 30) * July ** Lantern festival (July 25–27) ** Children’s lantern float offering (July 25) ** Great festival of purification (July 26) ** Great festival of the people’s association (July 26) ** Lantern dedication safety prayer (July 27) * October–November ** Shichi‑Go‑San prayers (October, November) * November ** Harvest festival (November 23) * December ** Emperor’s birthday festival (December 23) ** Year-end purification and New Year’s Eve festival (December 31)
== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.

[[ja:田村神社 (甲賀市)]] [[Tamura Shrine (Koka City)]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}
{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

==Overview== {{Infobox religious building | name = Tamura Shrine (田村神社) | image = File:Tamura jinja Honden.jpg | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] [[:en:Kōka, Shiga|Kōka City]] [[:en:Tsuchiyama, Shiga|Tsuchiyama Town]] {{ill|Kitatsuchiyama|de|Kitatsuchiyama|ja|土山町北土山|zh|土山町北土山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitatsuchiyama|1=Kitatsuchiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86737193}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.93056|N|136.29833|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|WD=Q941979}} | shrine_ranking = Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|de|Präfektur‑Schrein|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|县社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | established = Legendary: 3rd year of Kōnin (812) | main_shrine = Three‑bay [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|nagare‑zukuri]] | pilgrimage_site = {{ill|Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|de|Pilgerweg 134|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道 第134番|zh|神仏灵场巡拜之道 第134番|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2nd in Shiga) | annual_festival = [[:en:April 8|April 8]] | prefecture= {{ill|Koka|WD=Q847584}} }}
<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.

==Overview== {{Infobox religious building | name = Tamura Shrine (田村神社) | image = File:Tamura jinja Honden.jpg | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] [[:en:Kōka, Shiga|Kōka City]] [[:en:Tsuchiyama, Shiga|Tsuchiyama Town]] {{ill|Kitatsuchiyama|de|Kitatsuchiyama|ja|土山町北土山|zh|土山町北土山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitatsuchiyama|1=Kitatsuchiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86737193}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.93056|N|136.29833|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|WD=Q941979}} | shrine_ranking = Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|de|Präfektur‑Schrein|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|县社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | established = Legendary: 3rd year of Kōnin (812) | main_shrine = Three‑bay [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|nagare‑zukuri]] | pilgrimage_site = {{ill|Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|de|Pilgerweg 134|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道 第134番|zh|神仏灵场巡拜之道 第134番|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2nd in Shiga) | annual_festival = [[:en:April 8|April 8]] | prefecture= {{ill|Koka|WD=Q847584}} }}
<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Festivals == * Monthly ** Monthly festival (18th of each month) * January ** New Year service (January 1) ** New Year grand prayer (January 1–7) * February ** National Foundation Day service (February 11) ** Great Exorcism Festival (February 17–19) * April ** Annual festival (April 8) * June ** Great Purification (June 30) * July ** Lantern festival (July 25–27) ** Children’s lantern float offering (July 25) ** Great festival of purification (July 26) ** Great festival of the people’s association (July 26) ** Lantern dedication safety prayer (July 27) * October–November ** Shichi‑Go‑San prayers (October, November) * November ** Harvest festival (November 23) * December ** Emperor’s birthday festival (December 23) ** Year-end purification and New Year’s Eve festival (December 31)
== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.

==Overview== {{Infobox religious building | name = Tamura Shrine (田村神社) | image = File:Tamura jinja Honden.jpg | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] [[:en:Kōka, Shiga|Kōka City]] [[:en:Tsuchiyama, Shiga|Tsuchiyama Town]] {{ill|Kitatsuchiyama|de|Kitatsuchiyama|ja|土山町北土山|zh|土山町北土山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitatsuchiyama|1=Kitatsuchiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86737193}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.93056|N|136.29833|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|WD=Q941979}} | shrine_ranking = Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|de|Präfektur‑Schrein|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|县社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | established = Legendary: 3rd year of Kōnin (812) | main_shrine = Three‑bay [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|nagare‑zukuri]] | pilgrimage_site = {{ill|Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|de|Pilgerweg 134|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道 第134番|zh|神仏灵场巡拜之道 第134番|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2nd in Shiga) | annual_festival = [[:en:April 8|April 8]] | prefecture= {{ill|Koka|WD=Q847584}} }}
<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Festivals == * Monthly ** Monthly festival (18th of each month) * January ** New Year service (January 1) ** New Year grand prayer (January 1–7) * February ** National Foundation Day service (February 11) ** Great Exorcism Festival (February 17–19) * April ** Annual festival (April 8) * June ** Great Purification (June 30) * July ** Lantern festival (July 25–27) ** Children’s lantern float offering (July 25) ** Great festival of purification (July 26) ** Great festival of the people’s association (July 26) ** Lantern dedication safety prayer (July 27) * October–November ** Shichi‑Go‑San prayers (October, November) * November ** Harvest festival (November 23) * December ** Emperor’s birthday festival (December 23) ** Year-end purification and New Year’s Eve festival (December 31)
== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.

<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Festivals == * Monthly ** Monthly festival (18th of each month) * January ** New Year service (January 1) ** New Year grand prayer (January 1–7) * February ** National Foundation Day service (February 11) ** Great Exorcism Festival (February 17–19) * April ** Annual festival (April 8) * June ** Great Purification (June 30) * July ** Lantern festival (July 25–27) ** Children’s lantern float offering (July 25) ** Great festival of purification (July 26) ** Great festival of the people’s association (July 26) ** Lantern dedication safety prayer (July 27) * October–November ** Shichi‑Go‑San prayers (October, November) * November ** Harvest festival (November 23) * December ** Emperor’s birthday festival (December 23) ** Year-end purification and New Year’s Eve festival (December 31)
== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.

==Overview== {{Infobox religious building | name = Tamura Shrine (田村神社) | image = File:Tamura jinja Honden.jpg | location = [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] [[:en:Kōka, Shiga|Kōka City]] [[:en:Tsuchiyama, Shiga|Tsuchiyama Town]] {{ill|Kitatsuchiyama|de|Kitatsuchiyama|ja|土山町北土山|zh|土山町北土山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitatsuchiyama|1=Kitatsuchiyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q86737193}} | coordinates = {{Coord|34.93056|N|136.29833|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|WD=Q941979}} | shrine_ranking = Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|de|Präfektur‑Schrein|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|zh|县社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} | established = Legendary: 3rd year of Kōnin (812) | main_shrine = Three‑bay [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|nagare‑zukuri]] | pilgrimage_site = {{ill|Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|de|Pilgerweg 134|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道 第134番|zh|神仏灵场巡拜之道 第134番|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pilgrimage Route of Shinto Temples 134|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2nd in Shiga) | annual_festival = [[:en:April 8|April 8]] | prefecture= {{ill|Koka|WD=Q847584}} }}
<gallery> File:Tamura jinja koka.JPG|Stairway in front of the main hall File:Tamura jinja Torii.jpg|Torii gate </gallery>
'''Tamura Shrine''' ({{ill|Tamura Jinja|de|Tamura‑jinja|ja|田村神社|zh|田村神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamura Jinja|1=Tamura Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11576976}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in Tsuchiyama Town, Kōka City, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. The shrine held the rank of a former prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. The [[:en:Tōkaidō (region)|Tōkaidō]] passes through part of the approach from the first to the second torii and from the second torii to the {{ill|Kaido Bridge|de|Kaido‑Brücke|ja|海道橋|zh|海道桥|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaido Bridge|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
Every year, the shrine is famous for its Great Exorcism Festival ({{ill|yakuyoke taisai|ja|厄除大祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/yakuyoke taisai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) held over three days centered on [[:en:February 18|February 18]].
== History == On April 8 in the 45th year of Emperor Suinin’s reign, {{ill|Kakao|de|Kakao|ja|甲可翁|zh|甲可翁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakao|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined the spirit of [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Princess Yamatohime]] at {{ill|Kaka Hiunomiya|de|Kaka Hiunomiya|ja|甲可日雲宮|zh|甲可日云宫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaka Hiunomiya|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, naming it {{ill|Kōza Daimyōjin|de|Kōza‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座大明神|zh|高座大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – this is considered the origin of Tamura Shrine.
During the [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]], [[:en:Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro]] was ordered by [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]] to pacify the {{ill|evil spirits|de|Böse Geister|ja|悪鬼|zh|恶鬼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/evil spirits|1=evil ghosts|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11492603}} of {{ill|Mount Suzuka|de|Suzuka‑Berg|ja|鈴鹿峠|zh|铃鹿峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Suzuka|1=Suzuka Pass|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11649485}}. After swiftly subduing them, he shot an arrow and said, “By the merit of this arrow, may it ward off disaster for all people. Enshrine me where this arrow falls.” He thereafter had the main hall built at that spot.
In 812 (3rd year of Kōnin), by imperial decree of [[:en:Emperor Saga|Emperor Saga]], a sanctuary for Sakanoue no Tamuramaro was established on the twin peaks of Suzuka Pass<ref name="Kirimura2012">{{harv|Kirimura|2012|page=121}}</ref>. That same year, when an epidemic occurred nearby, the emperor ordered a grand exorcism rite at this shrine, leading to its veneration as a god of exorcism and, because Tamuramaro cleared the pass of evil spirits ensuring safe passage, as a protector of travelers.
On April 8, 822 (13th year of Kōnin), the sanctuary for Tamuramaro from the twin peaks was moved beside the original Kōza Daimyōjin and renamed {{ill|Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|de|Kōza Tamura‑Daimyōjin|ja|高座田村大明神|zh|高座田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
During the {{ill|Tenbun era|ja|天文|zh|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun era|1=Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q21096812}} wars, the shrine lost its Imperial plaque by Emperor Saga, but in 1638 (15th year of [[:en:Kan'ei|Kan’ei]]), it received a plaque inscribed {{ill|Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja|正一位田村大明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōichii Tamura Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from [[:en:Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Emperor Go‑Mizunoo]], which was affixed to the torii gate<ref name="miejinja">{{Cite web|title=〔甲賀〕 田村神社|publisher=Shiga Shrine Office|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/...|accessdate=2018-02-19}}</ref>. Throughout the Edo period, the Tamura clan, descendants of Tamuramaro and lords of the Ichinoseki Domain, continued to revere the shrine.
A temple, [[:en:Jingū-ji|Jingū-ji]], once stood as the shrine’s bettō temple, housing the thousand-armed Kannon statue created by {{ill|Enchin|ja|延鎮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchin|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 清水寺|1=Kiyomizu-dera|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q221716}} – Tamuramaro’s personal guardian Buddha – but in 1868 (Keiō 4), due to [[:en:Shinbutsu bunri|Shinbutsu bunri]], relations with the temple ended and the statue was moved to {{ill|Ei’un-ji|ja|永雲寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ei’un-ji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref>甲賀郡教育会『甲賀郡志 第3巻』(1926), 907頁</ref>.
In 1872 (Meiji 5), the shrine was renamed {{ill|Kōza Shrine|ja|高座神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōza Shrine|1=Takakura Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11669904}} and on April 6, 1887 (Meiji 20), officially renamed Tamura Shrine<ref name="#1"/> and designated a prefectural shrine.
In 1907 (Meiji 40), the Tamura Shrine on the twin peaks at Suzuka Pass was merged into {{ill|Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|ja|片山神社 (亀山市)|zh|片山神社 (亀山市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katayama Shrine (Kameyama)|qq=}} in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture.
The shrine treasures include the imperial arrowhead “{{ill|Chobaya no Mikura|ja|楚葉矢の御剣|zh|楚叶矢之御剑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chobaya no Mikura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}” and three arrowheads<ref name="#1"/>.

== Festivals == * Monthly ** Monthly festival (18th of each month) * January ** New Year service (January 1) ** New Year grand prayer (January 1–7) * February ** National Foundation Day service (February 11) ** Great Exorcism Festival (February 17–19) * April ** Annual festival (April 8) * June ** Great Purification (June 30) * July ** Lantern festival (July 25–27) ** Children’s lantern float offering (July 25) ** Great festival of purification (July 26) ** Great festival of the people’s association (July 26) ** Lantern dedication safety prayer (July 27) * October–November ** Shichi‑Go‑San prayers (October, November) * November ** Harvest festival (November 23) * December ** Emperor’s birthday festival (December 23) ** Year-end purification and New Year’s Eve festival (December 31)
== Sites of interest == * Exorcism drum bridge: Wooden bridge over the Tamura River<ref>{{Cite book|title=Aino Tsuchiyama History Guidebook|date=2015|publisher=Aino Tsuchiyama Fuchamoto Guide Association|page=9}}</ref> * Arrow bamboo * Kaido Bridge – from 1775 (An’ei 4) to 1939 (Shōwa 14), the Tōkaidō crossed the Tamura River on a floating board bridge at the shrine; depicted in Hiroshige’s “Spring Rain” of the series “The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō”. Rebuilt in July 2005 (Heisei 17) and named Kaido Bridge.
